name: Async Clipboard read
plain: Asks to read what is on the clipboard.
meaning: Can show anything the person copied: passwords, addresses, personal messages. Chromium asks permission; Firefox and Safari show a one-time Paste menu so the person approves each read.

access.prompt_ui: Chromium: permission prompt when document is focused. Firefox 125+ and Safari: floating Paste menu available after 1 second, skipped for same-origin content.
access.persistence: Chromium: persistent per origin; Firefox and Safari: none
steps: User gesture (transient activation) or Chromium grant
Promise resolves with text or ClipboardItems

limits.headline: Can see what you last copied, after you allow it or tap Paste
limits.user_action: You tap Paste on the page, or allow clipboard access when the browser asks
can: See text, images or other items you copied, one request at a time
Fill a form from what you copied
Show items you copied in any app, not just on this page
cannot: Peek at your clipboard in the background while you are in another tab or app
Get your clipboard in Chrome or Edge when the page is not in focus
Skip the small Paste button in Firefox and Safari; you tap it each time
Change your clipboard; that is a separate permission
limits.reach_label: Each time you allow or paste
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge ask once for permission. Firefox and Safari show a small Paste button you tap every time.

story.what_it_is: A site asks to read what you last copied.

marketing.name: Async Clipboard API
marketing.pitch: Google pitches modern clipboard access as a safer, asynchronous way to copy and paste images and text, with a permission prompt.

story.for_you: A prompt asks if the site may see text and images you copied. Safari and Firefox show a small Paste button instead. If you say no, the page cannot see your clipboard.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for paste buttons in editors and image tools, so users do not have to press keyboard shortcuts. It also powers paste from phone to desktop style features.

use_cases.example: A web design tool lets you paste an image you copied from another app straight onto the canvas.
A notes or spreadsheet web app pastes a copied table from a doc and keeps the layout.
A payment page reads a copied address or number to fill the form, saving typing errors.
A code editor in the browser pastes a snippet with formatting kept.
A chat web app lets you paste a screenshot from your clipboard to send it right away.
Malicious pages can try to read a copied password or crypto address if a person says yes.

risks: Could see passwords or private text

technical_bounds: Firefox and Safari do not support the clipboard-read permission name

abuse: Stealing passwords copied from a manager
